The legend of the pond

Every chain needs a folk hero. Ours just happens to have a bill.

Long ago, before candles were candles and charts were charts, the ponds of the Hood chain were ruled by fat carp who hoarded all the bread. Along came a duck in a little green hat, sunglasses on because eye contact is a form of consent, and a plan so simple it worked: waddle in, take a bite, share the loaf.

They called him Ducky. He didn't rob banks — he didn't need to, banks don't like water. Instead he found the driest, dustiest liquidity sitting in whale wallets and gave it wings. Or webbed feet. The metaphor gets wobbly, much like his walk.

Today $DUCKY carries on the tradition: every trade is a tiny heist, every holder is a merry duck, and every whale is politely, relentlessly, quacked at until they share. The loot doesn't sit in some dusty chest either — every fee $DUCKY collects gets converted straight into $MSTR stock token and dropped back into holder wallets. Robin Hood had a bow. Ducky has a bill and a distribution contract.

Questions, answered by a duck

He can't talk, but he can type, apparently.

Is this financial advice?

No. This is a duck in sunglasses. Please consult an actual professional, or at least someone taller than a duck, before making financial decisions.

Why "on Hood"?

Because that's the chain, and because a duck in a Robin Hood hat writes its own tagline. We just typed it up.

Is there a real Robin Hood involved?

Nope — just the hat, the hood chain, and the folk-hero bit. No brokerage, archer, or medieval outlaw was harmed or consulted in the making of this token.

What makes $DUCKY different from every other meme coin?

Statistically, very little. Emotionally, everything. He's got a hat. Show us another coin with a hat.

Can I add utility to $DUCKY?

You can absolutely try. The community is fully in charge of dreaming up utility. So far the leading proposal is "vibes," which is passing by a landslide.
